WHAT THIS IS

A trend-flip model across the whole watchlist. Two moving averages: when the fast one is above the slow one the model is LONG, otherwise FLAT. The page shows which state every ticker is in, how long it has been there, and - the number you act on - the price at which it would flip.

THE MODEL

SETTINGMA type and the fast/slow lengths, e.g. EMA 20/50. +r20 means a rate-of-change gate over 20 bars is also active.
MA TYPESMA, EMA, WMA or HMA. Which one is used is part of the search, not a fixed choice - they lag differently, and which lag suits a ticker is an empirical question.
ROC GATEThe derivative. The model only goes long if the slow MA is actually rising over the gate window, not merely below the fast one. This is what suppresses the whipsaws a bare crossover generates in a flat market.

EVERY COLUMN

STATELONG fast above slow and any gate passes. FLAT otherwise.
FLIPPEDThe state changed on the latest bar. Unlike a pivot model there is no confirmation lag - a crossover is known the moment the bar closes.
FLIP @The number you act on. The price at which the two MAs meet on the next bar. Above it the model is long, below it flat. Every MA here is a linear function of the next price, so this is solved exactly rather than searched.
%Distance from the current price to that level. Highlighted amber within 3%, which is the NEAR FLIP filter.
MA GAP %Separation between the two MAs as a percent of the slow one. A wide gap means a firmly established trend; near zero means the model is about to be indecisive.
SLOPE %How fast the slow MA is moving over the gate window. A LONG state on a flat slope is weaker than one on a rising slope.
BARS IN / SINCEHow long the current state has held, and when it started.
FLIPSTotal flips over the loaded history - a sanity check on whether the setting produces a sensible trade rate for this ticker.

THE OPTIMIZED SETTING

The DEFAULT / OPTIMIZED toggle switches between a plain EMA 20/50 for every ticker and a per-ticker setting found by grid search over MA type, fast length, slow length and ROC window. Selection uses only the first 70% of history; the remainder is scored afterwards and never influences the choice. The pick is the median score of its neighbouring length combinations, so a setting that only works at one exact pair is discarded.

Judge this model on drawdown, not just return. A long/flat trend model is not trying to out-earn buy and hold on something that went straight up - it cannot, because it is out of the market part of the time and its signals lag. It is trying to sidestep the falls. On a test tape that rose then crashed, the model returned +51% against -20% for holding, with a 6% drawdown against 60%.

So a ticker showing a negative edge but a much smaller drawdown is not a failure. The optimizer report prints both, and ranks on the blend of edge over buy and hold and return per unit of drawdown for exactly that reason.

The standing caveat. Per-ticker optimization has been tried repeatedly on this watchlist with other models and produced no out-of-sample edge each time. Trend following has a more plausible mechanism than mean reversion did, but nothing here proves it worked. Read the out-of-sample columns in the optimizer output before switching the toggle and leaving it there.

LIVE PRICES

When a live feed is attached, PRICE and the distance to FLIP @ update. STATE does not: a moving average needs a completed bar, and a state recomputed from a live tick would flicker across the flip level all session. What matters intraday is how close price is to the level, and that is live.

THE SIMULATOR

The SIMULATOR tab runs the flip signals through a full trade model with every setting adjustable - capital, fees on both sides, order trigger, entry sizing, exit type and size, and a start date. It opens on all-in / all-out, which is what a flip model means, but the sizing is adjustable like everything else. EXPORT JSON and COPY FOR BOT hand the whole snapshot - state, flip levels, recent signals and simulation results - to something else in one piece.
